title: Missing factor in (2x+p)(x+1)
source: Theory IGCSE-14.6 Quick check 1 (2x^2+3x+1=(2x+1)(x+1), so p=1); book Worked example 21 style, new numbers

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The constant term is \(p\), and \((2x+{p|int})(x+1)=2x^2+{B|int}x+{C|int}\), so \(p={p|int}\).
steps.note: p is the constant in the first bracket and equals the constant term.

title: Larger root after factorising a non-monic quadratic
source: Theory IGCSE-14.6 Quick check 2 (larger root of 3x^2-14x+8=0 is 4); book Worked example 21 style, new numbers
stem: The equation \(3x^2-{B|int}x+{C|int}=0\) factorises. What is the larger root?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(3x^2-{B|int}x+{C|int}=(3x-{p|int})(x-{q|int})\), so the roots are \(({p|int})/3\) and \({q|int}\). The larger root is \({q|int}\).
steps.note: q is chosen larger than p/3, so it is the larger root. Original: (3x-2)(x-4).

title: Product ac in the grouping method
source: Theory IGCSE-14.6 Quick check 3 (ac for 10x^2+11x-8 is -80); book Worked example 22 style, new numbers
stem: To factorise \({a|int}x^2+11x+{c|int}\) by grouping, you first compute the product of the coefficient of \(x^2\) and the constant term. What is that product?

steps.name: A
steps.note: This is the product ac used to search for a factor pair that adds to the middle coefficient.

title: Factorise a quadratic with leading coefficient not 1

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019), Question 7(c)(ii) only. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 7(c)(i), (iii) and (iv) are omitted.

stem:
This question is 0580/41/O/N/19 Question 7(c)(ii), taken from the official QP.

Factorise \(5x^2-23x+12\).  [2]

steps.name: B1
steps.text_tex: A correct pair of brackets with the same product of constants, or a correct grouping such as \(5x(x-4)-3(x-4)\), earns the first mark.
steps.note: MS: B1 for (5x+a)(x+b) with ab=12 or a+5b=-23, or for 5x(x-4)-3(x-4) or x(5x-3)-4(5x-3).

steps.name: A
steps.note: MS: (5x-3)(x-4) final answer, 2 marks. Independent check: (5x-3)(x-4)=5x^2-20x-3x+12=5x^2-23x+12.
